hero.filename: The Grave Stele of Demetria and Pamphile (4th cent. B.C.) at the Archaeological Museum of Kerameikos on 27 June 2018.jpg
hero.caption:
The inscription beneath the pediment gives the names of the two dead sisters. The women, remote and isolated, gaze apathetically at the spectator. They are already in another, transcendental world, far from the things of this life. The pilasters of the naiskos have been restored. It is one of the last tomb stones made before the law passed by Demetrius of Phaleron prohibiting the erection of luxurius tomb monuments. Ca. 325-310 B.C. From a grave enclosure by the South Way. Accession number: P 687. Archaeological Museum of Kerameikos. Athens, Greece. 
Text: Museum inscription.
